stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 2 x^{2} - 7 x + 1 \) and \( g(x) = 1 - x \). Find the exact total area of the regions between the graphs of f and g from \( x = -1 \) to \( x = \frac{7}{2} \).

worked_solution.text: \( f(x) - g(x) = 2 x \left(x - 3\right) \), so the graphs cross at \( x = 0 \) and \( x = 3 \), both inside the interval. f is above g before the first crossing and after the second, and below g between them.
worked_solution.rule_named: intersections and order of the curves

worked_solution.text: The pieces are \( \int_{-1}^{0} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{11}{3} \), \( \int_{0}^{3} \left(g(x) - f(x)\right)\,dx = 9 \) and \( \int_{3}^{\frac{7}{2}} \left(f(x) - g(x)\right)\,dx = \frac{5}{6} \).
worked_solution.rule_named: area of each piece, upper minus lower

worked_solution.text: The total area is the sum of the pieces, \( \frac{27}{2} \).

options.derivation: the crossing at x = 3 missed, so the second integral runs from 0 to 7/2 across it
f(x) - g(x) integrated once over the whole interval, across both crossings
the curves split correctly but each piece integrated as lower minus upper
